extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, Department of the Interior staff, tribal leaders and advocates seeking federal recognition, Congressional staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, evidentiary considerations, and procedural timelines for determining whether a group qualifies as a federally recognized Indian tribe (with focus on petitions to the Assistant Secretary/Secretary and historical/administrative precedents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary preliminary report requirement (54.10(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall make a preliminary written report to the petitioner of proposed findings and conclusions. This report must outline the evidence for this decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary report should set out the evidence relied upon so the petitioner knows the basis for the proposed determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner response period and right to oral argument (54.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the preliminary report, the petitioner shall have ninety (90) days to respond, including an opportunity to present oral argument to rebut the evidence relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners have a 90-day window to submit written rebuttal and to request/present oral argument addressing the evidence in the preliminary report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary final report timeline and publication (54.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall have thirty (30) days after petitioner's response to prepare a report of his findings and his final determination as to the petitioner's status; such report shall be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final determination by Assistant Secretary must be prepared within 30 days of the petitioner's response and be published publicly in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary review and possible supersession (54.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary's final determination shall be subject to review by the Secretary, who may, by acting within thirty (30) days of such publication, supersede that determination. If the Secretary takes no action within such 30-day period, the Assistant Secretary's determination shall be final and effective as of the date of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary has a 30-day window after Federal Register publication to review and overturn; absence of action makes the Assistant Secretary's decision final and effective from publication date. The petitioner may present its own response to the Secretary concerning the Assistant Secretary's determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary finality and notice when Secretary reviews (54.11(e)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the matter is reviewed by the Secretary, his determination shall be final. Notice thereof shall be given to the petitioner and published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Secretary acts, his determination is final and must be accompanied by notice to the petitioner and Federal Register publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of an affirmative determination—eligibility for services and sovereign privileges (54.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determination that the petitioner is an Indian tribe, the tribe shall be fully eligible for all services and benefits from the federal government available to other federally acknowledged tribes and entitled to all the privileges and immunities available to other federally acknowledged tribes by reason of their sovereign status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition confers eligibility for federal programs, services, treaty rights, and sovereign privileges comparable to other federally acknowledged tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary obligation to protect existing services and seek appropriations (54.11(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Secretary shall take all steps necessary to insure that appropriations for BIA programs and services provided as assistance and services to existing tribes will not be diminished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extending recognition, the Assistant Secretary must seek appropriations or take measures so that services to currently recognized tribes are not reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: C.F.R. Part 52.1 (historical definition of recognized tribe)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any Indian tribe which has entered into a treaty, convention, or executive agreement with the Federal government or whose Tribal entity has been otherwise recognised by the United States."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regulatory definition historically applied to tribes that voted on the Indian Reorganization Act; it is cited as an existing formal definition but limited in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felix Cohen criterion: treaty relations with the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: That the group has had treaty relations with the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of treaty relations is a strong indicator of tribal existence and carries weight in administrative determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felix Cohen criterion: denominated a tribe by Act of Congress or Executive Order
rubrics_metrics.description: That the group has been denominated a tribe by Act of Congress or Executive Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal legislative or executive acts recognizing the group as a tribe are dispositive evidence of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felix Cohen criterion: treated as having collective rights in tribal land or funds
rubrics_metrics.description: That a group has been treated as having collective rights in tribal land or funds even though not expressly designated a tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical treatment regarding collective land/fund rights supports recognition even absent explicit 'tribe' label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felix Cohen criterion: treated as a tribe or band by other Indian tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: That the group has been treated as a tribe or band by other Indian tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition by neighboring/related tribes (political/social treatment) is evidence of tribal identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felix Cohen criterion: exercised political authority over members
rubrics_metrics.description: That the group has exercised political authority over its members, through a tribal council or other governmental forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of internal political organization and governance (councils, decision-making structures) is a key factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: special appropriations or congressional acts for the group
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group has received special appropriations (or other direct congressional action) for the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congressional appropriations or special statutes specifically addressing the group indicate recognition or at least special federal treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: has now or ever received federal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group is now or has ever received federal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt of federal services historically (even if inconsistent) supports a claim of governmental acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: regular contacts with the group
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the BIA (or federal agencies) has had regular contacts with the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained administrative contact implies the government has treated the group as an entity deserving attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: frequent contacts with BIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group has had frequent contacts with the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent BIA interactions—records, visits, administrative dealings—serve as documentary evidence of a group's recognized status in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: organization meets regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group has an organization which meets regularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuing organized body that meets regularly demonstrates political and social continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: has a constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group has a constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written constitution or formal governing document is persuasive evidence of a tribal government's structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: elected tribal government approves membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group has an elected tribal government which approves membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated membership rules and an authority that enforces them are indicators of collective political identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: assertion of treaty rights (e.g., fishing rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group asserts treaty rights (for example, off-reservation fishing rights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active assertion or exercise of treaty rights, and legal participation to defend those rights, supports tribal existence and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix factor: recognition by Indian Claims Commission or other adjudicatory bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the group is recognized by the Indian Claims Commission (or similar adjudicatory body).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial recognition (claims adjudication, decisions) is strong evidence in favor of tribal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of administrative recognition (precedents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition may have been effected through Congressional statute, Solicitor's opinions, Deputy Commissioner letters, or Administrative Decisions (historical examples listed: Congressional statute; Solicitor's opinion; Deputy Commissioner's letter; Administrative Decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past administrative outcomes show multiple formal mechanisms for recognition; citing precedent (e.g., Mooksack recognized via Solicitor's Opinion) is important in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary types to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition determinations historically review ethnological, historical, legal, and political facts concerning each tribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comprehensive evidentiary record should include historical records, ethnographic data, evidence of political organization, congressional/agency actions, and treaty-related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual legal standard: recognition is acknowledgment, not creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal recognition is described as the Secretary's acknowledgement of the existence in fact of a tribal entity (not the creation of a tribe or the vesting of rights beyond those already generally available to Indian tribes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition acknowledges pre-existing political authority and confers the government's formal acknowledgment of that authority; it is a political act often characterized as a 'political question' for Congress and the Executive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical impacts/criteria to weigh when lack of recognition manifests
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical indicators of non-recognition's harms: lack of BIA protection of tribal government, loss of treaty fishing protection, denial by other federal agencies of program participation, denial of Indian Health Service benefits, BIA educational eligibility restrictions (blood quantum/residency rules), lack of tribal land base, inability to receive ICC awards in trust, inadequate housing and high rates of alcoholism/drug abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not evaluative 'tests' for recognition, these consequences are relevant contextual evidence of why recognition matters and may be used to document harm and necessity of recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reality: absence of official written criteria and risk of arbitrary decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of the Interior historically had no official written criteria to use as the basis for whether to extend political recognition to a tribal group, producing inconsistent or politicized decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should note the historic absence of codified standards and consider reliance on precedent, the Cohen factors, and a robust evidentiary record to guard against arbitrariness.
